proofs.proof_tex:
In \(\mathsf I_*\), \(L=\delta=0\) and \(x_i=0\), so the predictor-norm
constraints do not affect the objective.  By
\texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}, minimizing the epigraph variables first gives
\[
 \Gamma_s=z_B\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}
 \max_{h\in\{0,1\}}\lVert R_Qa_{1h}(w)\rVert_2. \tag{1}
\]
At calendar time \(2\), every relevant diagonal entry of \(R_Q\) is one.
Under nested support, write the early weights as
\((w_2,w_3,w_4)\).  The focal coordinate \((1,2)\) is distinct from the
three donor coordinates and has coefficient one.  Hence
\[
 \lVert R_Qa_{1,0}(w)\rVert_2^2
 =1+w_2^2+w_3^2+w_4^2. \tag{2}
\]
The simplex restrictions state separately that \(w_i\geq0\) and
\(w_2+w_3+w_4=1\).  Therefore
\[
 0\leq (w_2-w_3)^2+(w_2-w_4)^2+(w_3-w_4)^2
 =3(w_2^2+w_3^2+w_4^2)-1. \tag{3}
\]
Thus the sum of squares is at least \(1/3\), with equality if and only if
\(w_2=w_3=w_4=1/3\).  The optimized early nested variance is consequently
\(4/3\), and the displayed equal weights are its unique minimizer.

The deep early support is \(D_{1K}=\{3,4\}\).  For
\(w_3,w_4\geq0\) and \(w_3+w_4=1\),
\[
 \lVert R_Qa_{1,0}(w)\rVert_2^2
 =1+w_3^2+w_4^2
 =\frac32+\frac12(w_3-w_4)^2\geq\frac32. \tag{4}
\]
Equality holds if and only if \((w_3,w_4)=(1/2,1/2)\).

At time \(3\), both rules use \(D_{1,1}=D_{1K}=\{3,4\}\), and every
relevant diagonal entry of \(R_Q\) is \(1/10\).  Consequently,
\[
 \lVert R_Qa_{1,1}(w)\rVert_2^2
 =\frac1{100}(1+w_3^2+w_4^2)
 =\frac3{200}+\frac1{200}(w_3-w_4)^2
 \geq\frac3{200}, \tag{5}
\]
again with equality exactly at equal weights.  The positive early standard
deviations \(\sqrt{4/3}\) and \(\sqrt{3/2}\) both exceed the common late
standard deviation \(\sqrt{3/200}\).  Because \(\mathcal F_s\) is a product
of the two horizon-specific simplexes, the separate minimizers just found can
be selected simultaneously and minimize the maximum in (1).  Substitution of
the declared value \(z_B=9/4\) gives
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
 =\frac94\sqrt{\frac43}
 =\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}
 =\frac9{2\sqrt3},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}
 =\frac94\sqrt{\frac32}
 =\frac{9\sqrt6}{8}. \tag{6}
\]

The numerical enclosures require only exact rational squaring of positive
endpoints:
\[
 2.5980^2=6.749604<\frac{27}{4}<6.75012361=2.5981^2
\]
and
\[
 2.7556^2=7.59333136<\frac{243}{32}<7.59388249=2.7557^2.
\]
Thus
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\in[2.5980,2.5981],
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\in[2.7556,2.7557].
\]
Subtracting outward endpoints yields
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
 \in[2.7556-2.5981,\,2.7557-2.5980]
 =[0.1575,0.1577]. \tag{7}
\]
Finally, \(T_2=3\) implies \(2\in D_{1,0}\), because \(3>2\), whereas
\(2\notin D_{1,1}=D_{1K}\), because \(3\not>3\).  Hence the nested early
rule uses unit \(2\)'s untreated time-\(2\) outcome, while the common deep
pool excludes unit \(2\) at the early horizon solely because it adopts at the
late horizon.  Every donor simplex used above is nonempty, every variance is
strictly positive, and no limiting argument is used.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\).  Suppose
\(\mathcal E\ne\varnothing\), \(L=\delta=0\), \(\Sigma_Q\) is diagonal, and
the eligible row-cell sets are pairwise disjoint:
\(\mathcal C^s_e\cap\mathcal C^s_f=\varnothing\) whenever \(e\ne f\).
Then every \(v_{s,e}\) is attained and strictly positive, and \(W_s\) is the
unique positive number \(R_s\) satisfying
\[
 \prod_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{2\Phi\!\left(\frac{R_s}{\sqrt{v_{s,e}}}\right)-1\right\}
 =1-\alpha. \tag{8}
\]
If the displayed conditions hold for both support rules, then
\(v_{\mathrm{nested},e}\leq v_{\mathrm{deep},e}\) for every
\(e\in\mathcal E\).  If this inequality is strict for at least one
coordinate, then \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}<W_{\mathrm{deep}}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix a support rule \(s\) and an index \(e=(j,h)\).  Assumption
\texttt{ass:donor-feasibility} gives \(D_{jK}\ne\varnothing\), and
\(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\) follows from \(h\leq K\).  Hence the coordinate
simplex \(\Delta(D^s_e)\) is nonempty under either rule.  It is also compact.
The quadratic map
\[
 q_e(\omega):=a_e(\omega)^{\top}\Sigma_Qa_e(\omega)
\]
is continuous on that simplex, so the minimum defining \(v_{s,e}\) is
attained.  The declared positive definiteness of \(\Sigma_Q\) and the unit
coefficient of \(a_e(\omega)\) at its focal cell imply
\[
 q_e(\omega)>0
 \quad\text{for every }\omega\in\Delta(D^s_e),
 \qquad v_{s,e}>0. \tag{9}
\]

We next identify the coverage functional, keeping it distinct from the causal
target.  Under \(L=\delta=0\), \texttt{lem:bias-radius} gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}
 |a_e(w)^{\top}m|=0
\]
for every feasible \(w\) and every \(e\).  Therefore every law in the model
class has \(a_e(w)^{\top}m=0\).  By
\texttt{lem:prediction-error}, the estimation error vector
\[
 Z(w):=\widehat\tau(w)-\tau
\]
is consequently centered Gaussian with covariance
\(A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\).  This proves the relationship between the
observed-law error and the causal contrast \(\tau\); it does not define the
causal contrast by the Gaussian model.

For distinct \(e,f\in\mathcal E\), the rows \(a_e(w)\) and \(a_f(w)\) are
supported respectively on the disjoint sets \(\mathcal C^s_e\) and
\(\mathcal C^s_f\).  Since \(\Sigma_Q\) is diagonal,
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\{Z_e(w),Z_f(w)\}
 =a_e(w)^{\top}\Sigma_Qa_f(w)=0. \tag{10}
\]
All marginal variances are positive by (9).  Thus the joint Gaussian density
has diagonal covariance and factors as
\[
 \prod_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi q_e(w_e)}}
 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{z_e^2}{2q_e(w_e)}\right\};
\]
hence its coordinates are independent.  It follows, for every deterministic
half-width vector \(\ell\), that every law in the model class has the same
coverage probability
\[
 \Pr\{|Z_e(w)|\leq\ell_e\text{ for all }e\}
 =\prod_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{2\Phi\!\left(\frac{\ell_e}{\sqrt{q_e(w_e)}}\right)-1\right\}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Thus the infimum over laws in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} equals the
right-hand side of (11).

Fix \(R\geq0\) and restrict attention to rectangles satisfying
\(\max_e\ell_e\leq R\).  Each factor in (11) is nondecreasing in
\(\ell_e\), so replacing every half-width by \(R\) cannot reduce coverage and
does not increase the maximum half-width beyond \(R\).  For \(R>0\), the
factor as a function of a positive variance \(v\) has derivative
\[
 \frac{d}{dv}\left\{2\Phi(R/\sqrt v)-1\right\}
 =-Rv^{-3/2}\varphi(R/\sqrt v)<0. \tag{12}
\]
The feasible weight set is the Cartesian product of its coordinate simplexes,
and \(q_e(w_e)\) depends only on the coordinate weight \(w_e\).  Hence the
largest coverage attainable with maximum half-width at most \(R\) is
\[
 F_s(R):=prod_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{2\Phi\!\left(\frac{R}{\sqrt{v_{s,e}}}\right)-1\right\}, \tag{13}
\]
and it is attained by selecting a variance-minimizing weight independently in
every coordinate and setting every \(\ell_e=R\).  The same conclusion holds
at \(R=0\), when both sides of (13) are zero because
\(\mathcal E\ne\varnothing\).

Every \(v_{s,e}\) is positive and \(\mathcal E\) is finite and nonempty.
Therefore \(F_s\) is continuous on \([0,\infty)\), strictly increasing there,
\(F_s(0)=0\), and \(F_s(R)\to1\) as \(R\to\infty\).  Since
\(0<\alpha<1/2\), the intermediate-value theorem gives a unique positive
\(R_s\) with \(F_s(R_s)=1-\alpha\).  Equation (13) shows that a deterministic
linear rectangle with maximum half-width \(R\) can be honest if and only if
\(F_s(R)\geq1-\alpha\), equivalently if and only if \(R\geq R_s\).  The
minimizers used in (13) attain honesty at \(R_s\).  Taking the infimum in
\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} proves
\[
 W_s=R_s, \tag{14}
\]
and establishes (8).

Finally, for every \(e=(j,h)\), the support definitions give
\(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\), and hence
\[
 \Delta(D^{\mathrm{deep}}_e)
 \subseteq\Delta(D^{\mathrm{nested}}_e).
\]
Minimizing the same variance quadratic over these two sets yields
\[
 v_{\mathrm{nested},e}\leq v_{\mathrm{deep},e}. \tag{15}
\]
Suppose at least one inequality in (15) is strict and let \(R_D>0\) be the
deep root.  For fixed positive \(R_D\), (12) and (15) imply
\[
 F_{\mathrm{nested}}(R_D)
 >F_{\mathrm{deep}}(R_D)=1-\alpha.
\]
Strict monotonicity and (14) then give
\(W_{\mathrm{nested}}<R_D=W_{\mathrm{deep}}\).  No rank condition on
predictors, interiority of a weight vector, or limiting argument is used.
added_lemmas.justification: On the observable zero-bias, diagonal-covariance, row-disjoint subclass, the exact robust frontier is a computable one-dimensional root rather than only a constant-factor comparison.
added_lemmas.gap: The result uses the shrinking donor geometry as an input but does not identify this Gaussian width functional with any estimator analyzed by Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein.
added_lemmas.consumer: The root equation gives \(\texttt{scpi}\) and \(\texttt{augsynth::multisynth}\) an exact regression test for when a horizon-specific donor enlargement strictly reduces simultaneous width.

added_lemmas.statement:
For \(\mathsf I_*\), the coordinatewise minimum-variance vectors are
\[
 (v_{\mathrm{nested},(1,0)},v_{\mathrm{nested},(1,1)})
 =\left(\frac43,\frac3{200}\right),
 \qquad
 (v_{\mathrm{deep},(1,0)},v_{\mathrm{deep},(1,1)})
 =\left(\frac32,\frac3{200}\right).
\]
The exact frontiers are the unique positive roots of
\[
 \left\{2\Phi(R/\sqrt{v_{s,(1,0)}})-1\right\}
 \left\{2\Phi(R/\sqrt{3/200})-1\right\}=\frac{19}{20}.
\]
They satisfy the outward-rounded enclosures
\[
 W_{\mathrm{nested}}\in[2.263171468,2.263171469],\qquad
 W_{\mathrm{deep}}\in[2.400455838,2.400455839],
\]
and consequently
\[
 W_{\mathrm{deep}}-W_{\mathrm{nested}}
 \in[0.137284369,0.137284371].
\]
In particular, the witness has a strict exact-frontier gain as well as the
strict fixed-Bonferroni SOCP gain in \texttt{prop:strict-witness-gap}.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The definition of \(\mathsf I_*\) gives \(\mathcal E=\{(1,0),(1,1)\}\), so
the index set is nonempty.  Under nested support the eligible row-cell sets
are
\[
 \mathcal C^{\mathrm{nested}}_{(1,0)}
 =\{(1,2),(2,2),(3,2),(4,2)\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal C^{\mathrm{nested}}_{(1,1)}
 =\{(1,3),(3,3),(4,3)\}.
\]
Under deep support the first set loses only \((2,2)\), while the second set is
unchanged.  In either rule, the two sets are disjoint because their calendar
times differ.  Moreover, \(\Sigma_Q=R_Q^{\top}R_Q\) is diagonal, with
diagonal entries one on the time-\(2\) cells and \(1/100\) on the time-\(3\)
cells; its smallest and largest eigenvalues are therefore respectively
\(1/100\) and one.  The remaining subclass conditions
\(L=\delta=0\) are part of the witness definition.

The variance minimizations in \texttt{prop:strict-witness-gap}, together with
\texttt{def:coordinate-minimum-variance}, give
\[
 v_{\mathrm{nested},(1,0)}=\frac43,
 \quad v_{\mathrm{deep},(1,0)}=\frac32,
 \quad
 v_{\mathrm{nested},(1,1)}=v_{\mathrm{deep},(1,1)}=\frac3{200}. \tag{16}
\]
The hypotheses of \texttt{thm:disjoint-diagonal-exact-frontier} now hold for
both rules.  Substituting (16) and \(1-\alpha=19/20\) in (8) gives the two
displayed root equations.  Since \(4/3<3/2\), the strict-coordinate conclusion
of that theorem proves
\[
 W_{\mathrm{nested}}<W_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{17}
\]

For completeness, the numerical assertions are finite interval statements,
not floating-point premises.  Outward-rounded rational evaluation of
\(\Phi(x)=\tfrac12+(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_0^x e^{-t^2/2}\,dt\), using rational
Taylor enclosures with the next-term remainder after range subdivision, gives
the following rational product enclosures at the four rational endpoints:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
 (s,R)&
 \prod_{e\in\mathcal E}\{2\Phi(R/\sqrt{v_{s,e}})-1\}\\ \hline
 (\mathrm{nested},2.263171468)&
 [0.9499999999845,\,0.9499999999847]\\
 (\mathrm{nested},2.263171469)&
 [0.9500000000857,\,0.9500000000859]\\
 (\mathrm{deep},2.400455838)&
 [0.9499999999829,\,0.9499999999832]\\
 (\mathrm{deep},2.400455839)&
 [0.9500000000783,\,0.9500000000787].
\end{array} \tag{18}
\]
All endpoints in (18) are decimal representations of rationals; the algebraic
square roots are enclosed by exact rational squaring before the integral
evaluation.  Each lower evaluation is below \(19/20\), and each upper
evaluation is above \(19/20\).  Strict monotonicity of the root functions
therefore gives the two asserted width intervals.  Outward subtraction gives
\[
 [2.400455838-2.263171469,\,
   2.400455839-2.263171468]
 =[0.137284369,0.137284371],
\]
which proves the certified positive gap and the reported approximations.
added_lemmas.justification: The same rational staggered instance now certifies a strict gap in the causal band decision target \(W_s\), not merely in the Bonferroni surrogate \(\Gamma_s\).
added_lemmas.gap: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein supply the donor-set geometry only; the displayed exact-frontier values belong to this note's bounded-mean known-covariance experiment.
added_lemmas.consumer: The interval enclosures provide deterministic numerical regression tests for exact independent-Gaussian calibration in \(\texttt{scpi}\) and \(\texttt{augsynth::multisynth}\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Let \(N=4\), \(T=3\), \(K=1\), \(p=1\), \(T_1=2\), \(T_2=3\), and
\(T_3=T_4=\infty\).  Take \(\mathcal J=\{1\}\), \(x_i=0\) for all units,
\(L=\delta=0\), \(\alpha=1/20\), and \(z_B=9/4\) with a certified
Gaussian-tail enclosure.  Let \(R_Q\) be diagonal, with diagonal entry \(1\)
for every cell at time \(2\) and \(1/10\) for every cell at time \(3\), and
set \(\sigma_{\min}=1/100\) and \(\sigma_{\max}=1\).  Then
\(D_{1,0}=\{2,3,4\}\) and \(D_{1,1}=\{3,4\}\); the deep rule uses
\(\{3,4\}\) at both horizons.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The displayed diagonal factor already fixes the covariance eigenvalues, but the construction omitted the class parameters.  The corrected construction records \(\sigma_{\min}=1/100\) and \(\sigma_{\max}=1\) and verifies the covariance-band membership used by the witness.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
\(\mathsf{Data}=(N,T,K,p,T_{\mathrm{adopt}},x,L,\delta,\alpha,
\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max},R_Q,z_B,\mathsf{NonemptyCert},
\mathsf{TailCert})\), where all scalar and matrix entries are binary rationals
or integers, \(\mathsf{NonemptyCert}\) verifies
\(\mathcal J\ne\varnothing\), \(\mathsf{TailCert}\) consists of
outward-rounded rational interval proofs of the two inequalities in the
definition of \(z_B\), and the input length \(B\) is the total binary length
of this record.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The Gaussian maximum and \(q_\alpha(M)\) require \(M\geq1\).  A finite certificate that \(\mathcal J\ne\varnothing\) makes this domain condition part of the rational input rather than an implicit convention.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
On fixed inputs satisfying \texttt{ass:treated-set-nonempty}, for
\(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), solve
\(\Gamma_s=\min_{w,u,v,g}g\) subject to \(w\in\mathcal F_s\),
\(\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\rVert_2\leq u_{jh}\),
\(\lVert R_Qa_{jh}(w)\rVert_2\leq v_{jh}\), and
\(Lu_{jh}+\delta+z_Bv_{jh}\leq g\) for every
\((j,h)\in\mathcal E\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: If \(\mathcal E\) were empty, the epigraph variable would not define the advertised nonnegative maximum-width value.  Restricting the construction to the declared nonempty-treated-set inputs enforces \(M\geq1\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
On fixed inputs satisfying \texttt{ass:treated-set-nonempty}, for
\(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), define
\[
 W_s=\inf_{w\in\mathcal F_s,\,\ell\in[0,\infty)^M}
 \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
\]
subject to
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}
 P\{ |\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\leq\ell_e
       \text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}\geq1-\alpha,
\]
where \(w\) and \(\ell\) are functions only of the fixed design and model
inputs.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The maximum over band coordinates and the Gaussian-max calibration require a nonempty coordinate set.  The corrected construction states the fixed-design domain condition explicitly.

proposed_assumptions.reason: This fixed-design support condition is equivalent to \(M=|\mathcal E|\geq1\), which is required for the maximum-width objective and for evaluating \(q_\alpha(M)\).
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This condition only rules out the vacuous no-target design and does not imply any coverage, width, optimization, or strict-gap conclusion.

proposed.name: Support-rule donor and eligible row-cell sets
proposed.construction:
For \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\), define
\[
 D^s_e=
 \begin{cases}
 D_{jh},&s=\mathrm{nested},\\
 D_{jK},&s=\mathrm{deep},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad
 \mathcal C^s_e=
 \{(j,T_j+h)\}\cup\{(i,T_j+h):i\in D^s_e\}\subseteq\mathcal C.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: This definition makes the row-disjointness condition and the support-rule comparison mathematically explicit.

proposed.name: Coordinatewise simplex minimum variance
proposed.construction:
For an admissible fixed design and \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\),
define, for \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\),
\[
 v_{s,e}=\min_{\omega\in\Delta(D^s_e)}
 \left(\mathbf e_{(j,T_j+h)}-
       \sum_{i\in D^s_e}\omega_i\mathbf e_{(i,T_j+h)}\right)^{\!\top}
 \Sigma_Q
 \left(\mathbf e_{(j,T_j+h)}-
       \sum_{i\in D^s_e}\omega_i\mathbf e_{(i,T_j+h)}\right),
\]
where \(\mathbf e_c\) is the standard coordinate vector of
\(\mathbb R^{|\mathcal C|}\).  Equivalently,
\(v_{s,e}=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}a_e(w)^{\top}\Sigma_Qa_e(w)\), because the
row \(a_e(w)\) depends only on its coordinate weight.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This is the computable side of the exact-width characterization on the row-disjoint diagonal subclass.

proposed.statement: For \(\mathsf I_*\), equal early nested weights \((1/3,1/3,1/3)\) and equal deepest-pool weights \((1/2,1/2)\) are optimal. The late contrast variance is \(3/200\), while the optimized early variances are \(4/3\) under nested support and \(3/2\) under deep support. Hence \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}=3\sqrt3/2=9/(2\sqrt3)\in[2.5980,2.5981]\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}=9\sqrt6/8\in[2.7556,2.7557]\), so \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\in[0.1575,0.1577]\). The fixed-pool comparator excludes unit \(2\) from the early contrast solely because that unit adopts at the later horizon, whereas the nested rule uses its valid untreated outcome at time \(2\).
proposed.justification: A rational staggered instance gives an interpretable, interval-certified positive SOCP gap; the separate exact-frontier proposition establishes that this instance also has a strict \(W_s\) gap.
proposed.gap: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein motivate the shrinking donor geometry and focus their exposition and application on the deepest pool, while explicitly allowing their estimator to use horizon-varying donors; this proposition does not evaluate their estimator.
proposed.consumer: The instance is a deterministic SOCP regression test for \(\texttt{scpi}\) and explains when an early not-yet-treated cohort carries precision that a common support discards.

The paper offers non-asymptotic staggered synthetic-control prediction intervals, conic implementations, and uniform inference across post-treatment periods.
The paper derives finite-sample optimal confidence intervals for scalar linear functionals over convex regression classes under known-variance Gaussian errors.
The paper trades worst-case conditional imbalance against variance when constructing generalized optimal matching weights.
The paper constructs facial-reduced extended duals with strong duality when ordinary conic constraint qualifications fail.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient closed-cone conditions for Farkas lemmas and strong duality in second-order-cone programming.

prose_updates.tldr: Staggered adoption creates shrinking sets of not-yet-treated donors. Conditional on a nonempty rationally encoded fixed design, this note turns all treated-unit--horizon errors into one deduplicated Gaussian contrast vector, derives the exact worst-case bias radius, and chooses horizon-specific simplex weights with a fixed-Bonferroni SOCP. The resulting band is finite-sample honest and lies within a dimension-uniform factor of the best deterministic linear synthetic-control rectangle. On the zero-bias subclass with diagonal covariance and disjoint eligible row cells, the exact frontier \(W_s\) is the unique root of an explicit Gaussian-product equation; the two-horizon witness has both an interval-certified exact-width gap and an interval-certified \(\Gamma\) gap. The facial-reduction theorem separately gives a complete degeneracy-safe if-and-only-if certificate for strict \(\Gamma\) improvement. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein supply donor geometry only, not this statistical class or an evaluated estimator.

project_justification.gap: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein define the shrinking donor sets and focus their exposition and application on \(D_{jK}\), while explicitly noting that their estimator may use horizon-varying donors. This note uses that geometry but neither attributes its bounded-mean Gaussian class to them nor claims that either width program evaluates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik supply non-asymptotic simultaneous prediction and conic architecture but do not optimize the exact honest joint width over the two nested products of donor simplexes. Scalar convex-class interval theory does not give the independent-coordinate root characterization or the degeneracy-safe comparison of the two SOCPs.
project_justification.niche: Known covariance with a prespecified spectral band, rational fixed inputs, a nonempty treated set, and this note's bounded linear conditional-mean class isolate a finite-sample panel decision problem in which donor availability, worst-case bias, shared-cell covariance, multiplicity, and exact certification are explicit. The targets are the attainable honest-width frontier \(W_s\), its implementable fixed-Bonferroni surrogate \(\Gamma_s\), and auditable strict-improvement tests for each object on its proved domain.
project_justification.fill: The note derives a deduplicated contrast representation, an exact support-function bias radius, finite-sample honest SOCP bands, and a dimension-uniform comparison with the exact robust frontier. It identifies \(W_s\) exactly on the zero-bias diagonal row-disjoint subclass, proves a strict exact-width gain in the rational staggered witness, and proves a separate finite if-and-only-if facial-reduction certificate for strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on degenerate active faces.

sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed integer dimensions, deterministic adoption dates with \(\mathcal J\ne\varnothing\), rational predictors and class radii, a known rational covariance factor, and a certified rational Bonferroni multiplier.
sampling_model.units: The finite set \(\mathcal I\) contains treated, not-yet-treated, and never-treated units; repeated unit--calendar-time cells are deduplicated in \(Q\).
sampling_model.treatment: Adoption is absorbing and deterministic; \(D_{jh}=\{i:T_i>T_j+h\}\) identifies untreated donor outcomes at the relevant calendar time.
sampling_model.overlap: The treated set is nonempty, and every deepest donor pool \(D_{jK}\) is nonempty; nesting then makes every horizon-specific donor simplex feasible and gives \(M\geq1\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no random nuisance estimation: weights and half-widths depend only on fixed design and model inputs. Exact independent-Gaussian calibration is proved only on the diagonal row-disjoint subclass; general correlated Gaussian-max calibration remains a post-solve refinement.

prose_updates.related_work: Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, Section 2, paragraphs defining \(\mathcal D_{jk}\)) provide the shrinking-donor-set geometry and focus their exposition and application on the deepest pool \(D_{jK}\), while explicitly noting that their estimator may instead use horizon-varying donor sets. They do not supply this note's bounded-mean known-covariance class, and no theorem here evaluates or dominates their partially pooled estimator. Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Sections 4.4 and 6 and Supplemental Appendix S.6) provide prediction-error, simultaneous-coverage, and conic-programming architecture; the present frontier changes the decision variable and loss. Armstrong and Koles\'ar (2018, equation (13) and Sections 3.2--3.4) provide scalar worst-case-bias plus standard-error logic over a convex Gaussian regression class; the exact product-root theorem here concerns a rectangle of independent contrasts on different nested simplex faces. Kallus (2020) motivates the dual-norm bias--variance optimization analogy. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2015, Theorems 2 and 3) and Anderson (1955, Theorem 1) supply Gaussian comparison tools for the general constant-factor result, while the global spectral covariance band is this note's explicit finite-experiment restriction. Pataki (2013, Sections 3--4), Jeyakumar, Kum, and Lee (2008, Theorems 3.1 and 4.1), and exact real-algebraic elimination support the now-proved degeneracy-safe certificate theorem \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\). Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021), Cao, Lu, and Wu (2026), Cerulli (2024), and Wei, Park, Kalangi, and Huang (2026) address different prediction, long-panel, donor-selection, or calibration regimes.
prose_updates.interpretation: The strict witness isolates the value of an early donor that is untreated when the early effect is measured but adopts by the final horizon. Allowing that donor only where valid lowers the early minimum variance from \(3/2\) to \(4/3\) without changing the late variance \(3/200\). On the row-disjoint diagonal subclass, the exact Gaussian-product characterization converts that local variance reduction into a strict simultaneous-width reduction from approximately \(2.400455838\) to \(2.263171468\). This is a statement about deterministic linear bands in the declared experiment, not about the numerical output of an existing partially pooled synthetic-control estimator.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact robust frontier \(W_s\) and the implementable SOCP value \(\Gamma_s\) remain distinct. The rational witness now proves strict improvement for both, but the exact-\(W\) calculation uses \(L=\delta=0\), diagonal \(\Sigma_Q\), and pairwise disjoint eligible row-cell sets. Outside that subclass the paper proves weak support dominance and the dimension-uniform comparison, not that every strict \(\Gamma\) gap is a strict \(W\) gap. The facial-reduction equivalence \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\) concerns strict \(\Gamma\) improvement on arbitrary degenerate active faces. General correlated Gaussian-max calibration is still a post-solve refinement.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Finite-sample coverage, the covariance-domination sandwich, the constant-factor frontier, weak nested-support dominance, and the two-horizon strict witness are theorem-level results. On the zero-bias diagonal row-disjoint subclass, \(\texttt{thm:disjoint-diagonal-exact-frontier}\) characterizes \(W_s\) by an explicit product root, and \(\texttt{prop:strict-witness-exact-frontier-gap}\) gives a certified positive exact-width gap. The complete finite certificate on degenerate SOCP faces is proved by \(\texttt{thm:degenerate-iff-gap-certificate}\); it is not an open OEQ and is not a substitute for exact-\(W\) strictness. The covariance band is a prespecified restriction for the known-covariance finite experiment. Unknown covariance, random donor selection, outcome-dependent weights, general correlated exact calibration, and a direct comparison with the Ben-Michael--Feller--Rothstein partially pooled estimator are outside this version. When donor sets coincide, the two support rules reduce to the same problem; with one unbiased contrast, the SOCP reduces to a rationally certified classical known-covariance Gaussian interval.
